title: CCIP: predicting CTCF-mediated chromatin loops with transitivity.
authors: Wang, Weibing; Gao, Lin; Ye, Yusen; Gao, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文用随机森林预测CTCF介导的染色质环，虽涉及CTCF-DNA结合位点，但核心是染色质构象预测，缺乏TF-DNA三维互作建模与AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: MOTIVATION: CTCF-mediated chromatin loops underlie the formation of topological associating domains and serve as the structural basis for transcriptional regulation. However, the formation mechanism of these loops remains unclear, and the genome-wide mapping of these loops is costly and difficult. Motivated by the recent studies on the formation mechanism of CTCF-mediated loops, we studied the possibility of making use of transitivity-related information of interacting CTCF anchors to predict CTCF loops computationally. In this context, transitivity arises when two CTCF anchors interact with the same third anchor by the loop extrusion mechanism and bring themselves close to each other spatially to form an indirect loop. RESULTS: To determine whether transitivity is informative for predicting CTCF loops and to obtain an accurate and low-cost predicting method, we proposed a two-stage random-forest-based machine learning method, CTCF-mediated Chromatin Interaction Prediction (CCIP), to predict CTCF-mediated chromatin loops. Our two-stage learning approach makes it possible for us to train a prediction model by taking advantage of transitivity-related information as well as functional genome data and genomic data. Experimental studies showed that our method predicts CTCF-mediated loops more accurately than other methods and that transitivity, when used as a properly defined attribute, is informative for predicting CTCF loops. Furthermore, we found that transitivity explains the formation of tandem CTCF loops and facilitates enhancer-promoter interactions. Our work contributes to the understanding of the formation mechanism and function of CTCF-mediated chromatin loops. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code of CCIP can be accessed at: https://github.com/GaoLabXDU/CCIP. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
abstract_zh: 动机：CTCF介导的染色质环（chromatin loops）是拓扑关联结构域（topological associating domains）形成的基础，并作为转录调控的结构基础。然而，这些环的形成机制仍不清楚，且全基因组范围内对这些环的映射既昂贵又困难。受近期关于CTCF介导环形成机制研究的启发，我们探讨了利用相互作用的CTCF锚点（CTCF anchors）的传递性相关信息来通过计算预测CTCF环的可能性。在此背景下，当两个CTCF锚点通过环挤压机制（loop extrusion mechanism）与同一第三个锚点相互作用，并在空间上彼此靠近形成间接环时，就产生了传递性。结果：为了确定传递性是否对预测CTCF环具有信息价值，并获得一种准确且低成本的预测方法，我们提出了一种基于两阶段随机森林的机器学习方法，即CTCF介导的染色质相互作用预测（CTCF-mediated Chromatin Interaction Prediction, CCIP），用于预测CTCF介导的染色质环。我们的两阶段学习方法使我们能够利用传递性相关信息以及功能基因组数据和基因组数据来训练预测模型。实验研究表明，我们的方法在预测CTCF介导环方面比其他方法更准确，并且当传递性作为适当定义的属性使用时，对预测CTCF环具有信息价值。此外，我们发现传递性解释了串联CTCF环的形成，并促进了增强子-启动子相互作用。我们的工作有助于理解CTCF介导染色质环的形成机制和功能。可用性与实现：CCIP的源代码可在以下网址访问：https://github.com/GaoLabXDU/CCIP。补充信息：补充数据可在《生物信息学》在线版获取。
